verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 12–16 document the full cable routing: (1) Page 12 shows the AC cable path (orange annotated line) from rooftop down the building side, with LA marker (yellow dot) at roof level. (2) Page 13 (top) shows the AC cable continuing down the building exterior wall past an LG AC unit. (3) Page 13 (bottom) shows the cable entering the side passage with 'LA Pit' and 'DC Earth Pit' labeled. (4) Pages 14–15 show the cable path through the narrow side passage with earth cable routing (purple annotated lines). (5) Page 16 shows the terminal equipment cluster: 'Main Meter', 'Solar Meter and Enphase Accessories Box', and 'AC Earth Pit' — all in the side passage. Note: This is a micro-inverter (Enphase IQ8P) system; each panel has its own micro-inverter converting DC to AC on the roof. There is no DC string cable run or standalone DCDB — the AC cable run begins at the rooftop panels. The documented run is: roof panels (micro-inverters) → AC cable annotated down building exterior wall → side passage → Solar Meter/Enphase accessories box → Main Meter. The annotated routing lines appear continuous across pages 12–16 with no visible orphan ends or unexplained gaps.
verdicts.rationale: Cable routing is documented continuously across pages 12–16, tracing the full AC cable path from roof panels to the main meter. As a micro-inverter system, DC cable from panels to DCDB is not applicable — each panel has its own micro-inverter. No orphan ends or routing inconsistencies are visible in annotated routing diagrams. Route traverses building wall → side passage → meter location in a logical, continuous sequence.
